\chapter{Software Requirements}
\section{User Interactions / Use Cases}
FlakeTrace has two actors. A \textbf{Developer} invokes it directly against a failing test
they are investigating. A \textbf{CI Pipeline} invokes it the same way, on demand for a known
failing test rather than on every build --- Non-Functional Requirement NFR-1 (Section
\ref{ch4:sec:nfr}) is the reason: our stakeholders' own CI-time budgets rule out running it on
every successful build. Both actors drive the same seven use cases (Figure
\ref{ch4:fig:usecases}): submit a diagnosis request, through to receiving a typed certificate.

\section{Use Case Diagram}

Figure \ref{ch4:fig:usecases} shows the whole committed project, not only what Iteration 1
delivers: every use case carries the \texttt{<<iteration 1>>} stereotype because all seven are
implemented on \texttt{main} today, but the attached notes mark exactly which part of each
FR's full commitment is still FYP-2 work (container sandboxing, the filesystem resource
family, the cost-aware adaptive search policy, and NFR-2's clean-machine deployment check) ---
checked against the real code (\texttt{runner/}, \texttt{evidence/}) while drawing this
diagram, not assumed from the proposal.
\section{Detailed Use Cases}
Table \ref{ch4:tab:usecases} summarises each use case from Figure \ref{ch4:fig:usecases}: who
starts it, what it does, and which functional requirement it traces to. UC2--UC6 are not
started directly by an actor --- they are \texttt{<<include>>}d in sequence by UC1, as the
diagram shows. Full use-case descriptions (preconditions, main flow, postconditions) are in
Appendix \ref{app:requirements}, Section \ref{appb:sec:usecases}, to keep this chapter
readable.

\begin{table}[H]\centering
\caption{Use cases, actors and functional-requirement trace}\label{ch4:tab:usecases}
\begin{tabular}{p{1.4cm}p{2.6cm}p{7.2cm}p{1.3cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{ID} & \textbf{Actor(s)} & \textbf{Description} & \textbf{Traces to} \\
\midrule
UC1 & Developer, CI Pipeline & Submit a diagnosis request: a pinned commit, Maven module,
  target test and execution budget & FR-1 \\
UC2 & (included by UC1) & Run the declared test order in one fresh JVM & FR-2 \\
UC3 & (included by UC2) & Collect resource events (static fields, system properties) for
  that run, attributed to the test methods involved & FR-3 \\
UC4 & (included by UC3) & Rank and run candidate predecessors to find the one(s) that
  reproduce the failure & FR-4 \\
UC5 & (included by UC4) & Minimise the reproducing order to a 1-minimal sequence and verify
  it with repeated clean replays & FR-5 \\
UC6 & (included by UC5) & Receive the Verified / Candidate / Unresolved certificate with its
  typed reason and evidence & FR-6 \\
UC7 & Developer, CI Pipeline & Invoke FlakeTrace via its CLI and consume a CI-compatible exit
  code & FR-7 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
